title: Pig Vagus Nerve Collection and Histological Processing
author: J. Ashley Ezzell
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6bqhamw
materials: We rinsed each sample with deionized water.
We rinsed the slides in distilled water.

steps.title: Collect Pig Vagus Nerve Samples
steps.instruction: Harvest vagus nerve samples from euthanized Yorkshire pigs.

substeps.instruction: Collect bilateral carotid sheath samples (2 cm length) at the level midway along the rostocaudal line from the rostral end of the sternum to the line connecting the left and right angles of the mandible (typically ~12 to 14 cm apart), measuring from the 'valley' of the common carotid bifurcation to the center of each sample.

Collect ~2 cm samples of the anterior and posterior subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve trunks along the esophagus, approximately halfway between the diaphragmatic esophageal hiatus and the gastroesophageal junction.
Dye the rostral end of each sample green to maintain orientation.
Place each sample between two histology sponges in a mega-sized histology cassette.
Store cassettes in a tub with 4% paraformaldehyde in a 4 °C refrigerator.

steps.title: Collect Rat Vagus Nerve Samples
steps.instruction: Harvest vagus nerve samples from rats following perfusion.

substeps.instruction: Perfuse rats with ~300 mL 1x PBS (until liver is cleared), followed by ~300 mL 4% paraformaldehyde (until joints and tissues are stiff).

Collect bilateral carotid sheath samples from the clavicle up to where the nerve and carotid intermingle with non-parallel other nerves, measuring from the 'valley' of the common carotid bifurcation to the center of each sample.
Collect the esophagus from the diaphragm to the stomach with the subdiaphragmatic vagus nerves attached.
Dye the rostral end of each sample green to maintain orientation.
Place each sample between two histology sponges in a mega-sized histology cassette.
Store cassettes in a tub with 4% paraformaldehyde in a 4 °C refrigerator.

steps.title: Tissue Processing and Embedding
steps.instruction: Process samples using a tissue processor and embed in paraffin.

substeps.instruction: Process samples on the long cycle in a Leica ASP300S Tissue Processor for ~10 hours using the following sequence: 70% ethanol (30 min), 80% ethanol (35 min), 95% ethanol (40 min x 4), 100% ethanol (40 min x 3), Clearite (50 min x 3), and paraffin wax (50 min x 3).
Cut each sample in half transversely and embed the halves together cut side down in paraffin to allow transverse sections starting from the center moving outward.

steps.title: Sectioning and Slide Preparation
steps.instruction: Collect tissue sections and prepare slides.

substeps.instruction: Collect 5 µm sections, placing two serial sections per microscope slide for fifteen slides.
Air dry slides overnight at room temperature.
Bake slides at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Masson's Trichrome Staining
steps.instruction: Stain selected slides (e.g., slides 2 and 14) using Masson's trichrome.

substeps.instruction: Bake slides at 60 °C for 1.5 hours, then cool overnight.
Deparaffinize and hydrate to distilled water: xylene (2x 6 min), 100% ethanol (5 min), 95% ethanol (4 min), 70% ethanol (3 min), dH2O (2x 1 min).
Place slides in Bouin's fixative (mordant) at room temperature overnight.
Wash in running tap water until yellow color disappears (~10 minutes).
Place in Weigert's Iron Hematoxylin solution for 10 min.
Wash in running tap water for 10 min.
Place in Biebrich Scarlet-Acid Fuchsin solution for 5 min.
Wash in running tap water for 2 min.
Place in Phosphomolybdic-Phosphotungstic Acid solution for 10 min.
Transfer directly to Aniline Blue solution for 3 min.
Differentiate counterstain in 1% Acetic Acid solution for 1 min.
Dehydrate, clear, and coverslip: 95% ethanol (1 min), 100% ethanol (4 min), xylene (5 min).

steps.title: Microscopy Imaging
steps.instruction: Image the processed samples using a microscope.

substeps.instruction: Image samples at 10x using a Nikon Ti2 microscope with a Photometrics Prime 95B-25MM camera.
Select the best of four slices per sample based on quality (no tearing or fraying).
